items.text: A's H1 element is empty, while B's H1 contains a full headline.
items.evidence: A h1.text = ""; B h1.text = "Payment Processing Made Simple (& Cheaper)"

items.text: The two sides use different document titles. A uses a descriptive phrase, and B uses a brand-pipe-slogan pattern.
items.evidence: A title "Payment Processing & Merchant Services"; B title "Merchant Savvy | Payment Processing Made Simple (& Cheaper)"

items.text: B's H1 is much larger and heavier than A's (empty) H1, and it is white on a dark background.
A uses web fonts (mainly Open Sans and Roboto, plus Calibri and icon fonts). B uses only the system-ui font stack.
items.evidence: A fonts: Open Sans 534, roboto 438, Roboto 140, calibri 134, Font Awesome 5 Free 18, eicons 2; B fonts: system-ui 136

items.text: H2 headings are about the same size, but B sets them bold where A uses medium weight.
items.evidence: A h2 28px weight 500; B h2 28.8px weight 700; visually A 'Payment Processing' is regular grey-black and B is heavy navy

items.text: A's body text is a light grey. B's body text is a dark navy.
items.evidence: A body_color rgb(146,146,146); B body_color rgb(28,29,58)

items.text: B's hero has a large indigo background with a diagonal gradient that lightens toward the bottom right.
items.evidence: B top_backgrounds rgb(30,34,140); gradient_backgrounds 4; B_slice_00 hero shading

items.text: B places the payment-logo strip inside a white rounded card next to the hero CTA. In A, that same image sits mid-page (in the empty top area).
items.evidence: B msuk-payment-logos rect x329 y557 300×50; A same file at x848 y1356

items.text: B has a visible top nav with dropdown chevrons ('Merchant Accounts', 'Card Machines', 'Online') and a dark pill 'Quotes' button. No nav is visible in A's screenshots, even though A has 4 nav elements in the DOM.
items.evidence: B_slice_00 header; A semantic nav 4 but nothing rendered in A_slice_00

items.text: B's logo is shown at a usable size. A's logo is measured at only 48×11px.
items.evidence: A merchant_savvy_purple.svg rect 48×11; B merchant-savvy-purple.svg rect 157×36

items.text: A shows category links as plain text lists in two columns with chevron icons, beside each section's heading and description. B shows them as bordered card tiles in a grid, each with an arrow icon.
items.evidence: A_slice_01 chevron lists; B_slice_00/01 bordered tiles with → arrows

items.text: B uses CSS grid for layout. A uses only flexbox.
items.evidence: A display_grid 0, display_flex 179; B display_grid 12, display_flex 17

items.text: B gives the Finance & Banking section a pale lavender-grey band to separate it. In A, every section sits on white.
items.evidence: B background rgb(244,245,251); B_slice_00 bottom and B_slice_01 top band

items.text: B replaces the missing stats images with indigo gradient panels that each hold a white line icon (phone, shopping cart, monitor).
items.evidence: B svgs 3 with rect/path/circle; B_slice_01 Mobile Payments, Mobile Ecommerce, Remote Working cards

items.text: B shows Research & Stats as bordered cards in a 4-column grid: an image area on top, a bold caption below, and 5 cards in total that wrap onto a second row.
items.evidence: B_slice_01: UK SMEs, Mobile Payments, Mobile Ecommerce, Remote Working, Payment Fraud

items.text: Real stats images display larger in B than in A.
items.evidence: charts.jpg A 208×139 vs B 263×175; payment-fraud-stats.jpg A 208×139 vs B 263×175

items.text: B gives the decorative stats images empty alt text. A uses filename-derived alt text prefixed 'Homepage (New Design)'.
items.evidence: B charts.jpg alt ""; A charts.jpg alt "Homepage (New Design) charts"

items.text: B uses the landmark elements header, main and footer. A has none of these, relying on nav and section.
items.evidence: A header 0, main 0, footer 0, section 15, nav 4; B header 1, main 1, footer 1, section 3, nav 1

items.text: A uses 0px or small (1–7px) corner radii. B consistently uses 8–15px radii on its cards and buttons, plus pill shapes.
A has some box shadows and transforms. B has no shadows or transforms and uses thin borders instead.
items.evidence: A box_shadows 12, transforms 6; B box_shadows 0, transforms 0; B tiles show 1px light borders

items.text: B's footer has a thin top divider and more spacing, and its links are indigo. A's footer copyright lines sit close together, with cyan links.
items.evidence: B_slice_01 hairline at y≈882, footer lines spaced; A_slice_02 copyright lines at ~14px spacing, links rgb(19,175,240)

items.text: Both footers end with the same 528×23 payment-types logo strip, left-aligned.
items.evidence: A payment-types-top.png 528×23 at x171; B payment-types.png 528×23 at x160

items.text: A's page is wider and taller than B's.
Both pages use a left content edge of about 160px.
items.evidence: A headings at x≈160 in A_slice_01; B logo x160 and headings x≈160

items.text: B has more visible text than A, mostly from the hero and benefit bullets. A contains one emoji character.
items.evidence: A words 131, emoji 1; B words 188, emoji 0

items.text: B has a real button element (a 'Menu' toggle) and some ARIA. A has no button elements but many more ARIA attributes.
items.evidence: A buttons 0, aria_attrs 96; B buttons 1 (primary_button 'Menu', radius 8px), aria_attrs 7

items.text: B uses bold dark-navy text for link labels on its tiles. A's link labels are regular-weight cyan text.
items.evidence: B_slice_00 'Merchant Account Providers' bold navy in tile; A_slice_01 same label regular cyan

items.text: A's heading outline jumps from an empty H1 to H3s that read like internal labels. B's outline is just H1 → three H2s.
items.evidence: A outline: h1 '', h3 'Desktop - Organic (+ types)', h3 'Mobile - IMS with Types', h2×3; B: h1 + h2×3

items.text: A's first screenshot slice is entirely blank white. No header, hero, logo or navigation is visible, and the first content starts below roughly 1300px. B opens with a header, a hero banner and a call to action in the first screen.
items.evidence: A_slice_00.png is blank. B_slice_00.png shows a logo/nav bar at the top and a blue hero. A page_height is 2877 and B page_height is 2419.

items.text: The palettes differ. A is mostly white with accents of light blue-grey (218,228,232), green (69,187,92), violet (71,55,255) and orange (249,66,19), but most of these are not visible in the render. B uses a tight palette of navy/indigo (30,34,140), amber (244,180,60), pale lavender-grey (244,245,251) and white.

A relies on a large external CSS framework with many classes and 304 inline style attributes. B uses 33 class uses (19 unique), a single style block and no inline styles. Neither uses utility classes, since tailwind-like fraction is about 0.
items.evidence: A classes total 2572 / unique 416, inline_style_attrs 304, stylesheets 44. B classes total 33 / unique 19, inline_style_attrs 0, stylesheets

items.text: B uses a larger vertical rhythm with clearly spaced sections and consistent 16px gaps between cards. A has large unexplained vertical gaps: ~1300px of blank space at the top and ~500px between the research images and their captions.
items.evidence: A_slice_00 blank, A_slice_01 gap between y≈770 and ≈1290. B slices have continuous content from the top.

items.text: B uses small inline SVG icons: yellow circular check marks for the hero bullets, arrows in cards, chevrons in nav, and phone, cart and monitor tiles. A uses icon fonts (Font Awesome 5 Free on 18 elements, eicons on 2) for the chevron bullets, and has 1 SVG.
items.evidence: B svg=3 (with rect, path, circle). A svg=1 and i=20.

items.text: Link density and nav depth differ. A has 105 anchors and 4 navs, with 56 ul and 227 li. B has 35 anchors, 1 nav, 11 ul and 40 li. The visible nav in B has only three top-level items.
items.evidence: A tag_counts: a 105, nav 4, ul 56, li 227. B: a 35, nav 1, ul 11, li 40.

features.statement: Hero headline is a large, bold, white H1 on a dark background, filled with a full benefit-style tagline.
Document title follows a brand-pipe-slogan pattern combining the brand name with a tagline.
Typography relies solely on the system-ui font stack rather than web fonts.
Section headings are set in bold weight (700) rather than medium weight.
Body text is dark navy rather than light grey, giving strong contrast.
Hero uses a deep indigo background with a diagonal gradient lightening toward one corner.
Palette is tight: navy/indigo, amber accent, pale lavender-grey and white.
A logo strip sits inside a white rounded card beside the hero call to action.
Header shows a visible top nav with few items, dropdown chevrons and a dark pill CTA button.
Logo is displayed at a clearly legible size in the header.
Category links appear as bordered card tiles in a grid, each with an arrow icon and bold navy label.
Layout uses CSS grid for card and section arrangements.
A pale lavender-grey background band separates one section from white sections.
Missing imagery is replaced by indigo gradient panels holding white line icons.
Stats appear as bordered cards in a multi-column grid with image on top and bold caption below, wrapping to a second row.
Decorative images carry empty alt text.
Page uses landmark elements header, main and footer with a clean heading outline of H1 then H2s.
Cards and buttons consistently use 8–15px corner radii, with some pill shapes.
Depth comes from thin 1px light borders with no shadows or transforms.
Footer has a thin top divider, generous spacing and indigo links.
First screen opens with header, hero banner and a call to action, with continuous content and no blank gaps.
Hero includes benefit bullets with yellow circular check icons, adding more visible persuasive copy.
Icons are small inline SVGs (checks, arrows, chevrons) rather than icon fonts.
Styling is lean, using few classes, one style block and no inline styles.
Page includes a real button element for the menu toggle, with minimal ARIA.
